newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Gonzalez says no comeback unless polls early.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Gonzalez says no comeback unless polls early.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister and Socialist party leader Felipe Gonzalez, who led Spain for 13 years, has said he will not run for top office again unless the present conservative government calls early elections.

Asked whether he would campaign again, Gonzalez said in a television interview on Tuesday: "I hope not and I hope that the government doesn't get nervous and speed up events, because then, perhaps, there will be no choice."
The next elections are scheduled for the year 2000.

Gonzalez surprised Socialist party faithful last Friday by resigning as leader after 23 years in the post, but many have questioned whether his retirement from the political front line would be permanent.
His resignation came just over a year after his general election defeat by Jose Maria Aznar's centre-right Popular Party.
Most Spaniards believe the decision is temporary, according to an opinion poll published on Tuesday by El Pais newspaper.
The poll showed that 70 percent of those questioned believed the charismatic Gonzalez would return to a leading role in the country.
The ex-premier told Antena 3 television on Tuesday night: "An electoral campaign is preceded by citizens getting to know those who are running.

"If my successor is not sufficiently established in the public eye we would be competing with a silly disadvantage. If one believes in one's political project and in one's ideas, there is no reason to give away this advantage."
The Socialist party congress lastr weekend voted in Joaquin Almunia, formerly party parliamentary spokesman, ex-minister and a long-time Gonzalez loyalist, to take over the leadership.
"In principle, it will be he who leads the debate. That is why he is head of the opposition and the party," Gonzalez said.
